Settings.Title: Traffic Lights & Lanes
Settings.AutoManageAll.Label: Manage all traffic lights automatically
Settings.AutoManageAll.Description: TLL takes over every signalled junction, builds a phase plan from its layout and adjusts the timing to the measured traffic. Junctions you configured yourself are left alone. Level crossings and movable bridges stay with the game.
Settings.AutoMode.Label: Control mode for automatic junctions
Settings.AutoMode.Description: Automatic: the autopilot decides; junctions outside green waves run adaptive. Adaptive: the phase with the most pressure goes next, and green adapts to traffic. Actuated: phases in fixed order, skipped without demand, green ends when the queue is gone. Fixed time: fixed greens, optimised every few minutes. Drain: every green runs until its queue has left or the exit backs up, at most 90 s.
Settings.AutoLayout.Label: Phase layout for automatic junctions
Settings.AutoLayout.Description: Automatic: the autopilot compares all layouts, each with and without a pedestrian scramble, with the traffic measured at each junction over days and picks the one with the least waiting. Permissive: oncoming traffic runs together, turning traffic gives way. Protected turns: turns across oncoming traffic get their own green. Split: one approach at a time. Permissive with a pedestrian scramble: plus a phase in which only pedestrians walk, in all directions.
Settings.AutoFlash.Label: Flashing yellow at low traffic
Settings.AutoFlash.Description: When a junction is quiet enough for priority rules, its signals flash yellow: the main road passes, the side roads give way. Signals come back as traffic grows. Separate thresholds for on and off keep it from flickering.
Settings.AutoLaneArrows.Label: Lane arrows by traffic
Settings.AutoLaneArrows.Description: The autopilot gives the lanes of each approach to the directions that need them, without paths crossing inside the junction. At signals it picks the split with the least waiting time under the best phase layout; one lane for straight and left traffic together exists there only where the approach has just one lane. Without signals it relieves the fullest lane. It changes only where it clearly helps, and leaves approaches where you connected lanes yourself.
Settings.AutoPrioritySigns.Label: Priority roads by traffic
Settings.AutoPrioritySigns.Description: At junctions without signals, the game decides right of way by the kind of road. Where one pair of approaches carries most of the traffic, it gets a priority road and the other approaches give way, also where the main flow turns. It works from the game's own traffic count. Each junction is reviewed every six game hours; junctions where you set signs yourself are left alone.
Settings.AutoTurnBans.Label: Forbid U-turns where they slow a junction
Settings.AutoTurnBans.Description: A U-turn that shares its lane with straight or left-turning traffic often keeps that traffic from its green, even when hardly anyone turns. At automatic junctions the autopilot forbids U-turns where the junction saves more waiting time than the detours of those who turned cost. A vehicle with no other way may still turn. In the panel you can allow or forbid each turn yourself.
Settings.TurnOnRed.Label: Turn on red by the autopilot
Settings.TurnOnRed.Description: The autopilot allows turning on red at automatic junctions where its estimate says it saves time. Right turns (left turns in left-hand traffic) then stop at red and go when the way is clear; only where they meet nothing but traffic they give way to, and never during a pedestrian scramble. At your own junctions, switch it in the panel.
Settings.EmergencyGreenWave.Label: Green wave for emergency vehicles
Settings.EmergencyGreenWave.Description: Ambulances, fire engines and police on a call get green for their direction at every TLL signal on their route, about 30 seconds before they arrive, until they have passed. The running green ends after its minimum for it.
Settings.KeepClear.Label: Keep junctions clear
Settings.KeepClear.Description: A lane stays red while its exit is backed up to the junction, so nobody gets stuck in the middle and blocks the cross traffic.
Settings.AutoGreenWaves.Label: Automatic green waves
Settings.AutoGreenWaves.Description: Finds main roads with signals close together and times them as green waves in both directions. Recalculated every few minutes from the measured traffic.
Settings.ShowProblems.Label: Mark problem junctions
Settings.ShowProblems.Description: Red rings on managed junctions where traffic queues up in the rush hour, from TLL's long-term measurement.
Settings.ShowCongestion.Label: Mark congestion
Settings.ShowCongestion.Description: Colours roads red where traffic flows slowly over the day, from the game's own traffic flow data.
Settings.TogglePanelBinding.Label: Open and close the TLL window
Settings.TogglePanelBinding.Description: Opens or closes the Traffic Lights & Lanes window.
Settings.PlannerUndoBinding.Label: Planner: undo
Settings.PlannerUndoBinding.Description: Takes back the last change in the planner, while it is open.
Settings.PlannerRedoBinding.Label: Planner: redo
Settings.PlannerRedoBinding.Description: Does again what Undo took back, while the planner is open.
Settings.PlannerCopyBinding.Label: Planner: copy the plan
Settings.PlannerCopyBinding.Description: Puts the plan open in the planner on the clipboard, to paste it at another junction or share it.
Settings.PlannerPasteBinding.Label: Planner: paste a plan
Settings.PlannerPasteBinding.Description: Loads a plan from the clipboard into the planner, turned to fit the junction. Nothing changes on the road until you apply it.
Settings.PlannerApplyBinding.Label: Planner: apply
Settings.PlannerApplyBinding.Description: Applies the plan open in the planner, if the check finds no error.
Settings.ResetAllToAutomatic.Label: Reset all junctions to automatic
Settings.ResetAllToAutomatic.Description: Junctions you set yourself, and ones you returned to the game, get the automatic control and a generated phase plan again. The traffic measured so far is kept, so the autopilot decides with it at once. Switches the city-wide automation on.
Settings.ResetAllToAutomatic.Warning: Reset all junctions to automatic? Your own settings and phase plans are lost.
Settings.ReleaseAll.Label: Return all junctions to the game
Settings.ReleaseAll.Description: Removes TLL's control from every junction, including the ones you configured. The game rebuilds its own signal groups.
Settings.ReleaseAll.Warning: Return all junctions to the game's control? Your own phase plans are lost.
Settings.ResetLanes.Label: Reset all lane rules
Settings.ResetLanes.Description: Removes all of TLL's turn bans, priority signs and lane connections, yours and the autopilot's, and switches both lane autopilots off. The game builds the lanes of those junctions anew. Run it once and save before removing TLL.
Settings.ResetLanes.Warning: Remove all of TLL's lane rules? Your own connections and signs are lost.
Settings.RebuildVanilla.Label: Repair signal data from other mods
Settings.RebuildVanilla.Description: Makes the game rebuild the signal groups of every junction TLL does not manage. Use it once after removing another traffic light mod, whose settings can stay behind in the save.
Settings.RebuildVanilla.Warning: Rebuild the signal groups of all junctions not managed by TLL?
Settings.VerboseLogging.Label: Detailed log
Settings.VerboseLogging.Description: Writes one line per junction plan to Logs/TLL.log. Useful when reporting a problem.
Settings.WriteMetrics.Label: Record metrics
Settings.WriteMetrics.Description: Writes measurements of every junction to ModsData/TLL/Metrics, one folder per game session: traffic and waiting per round, greens and why they ended, the autopilot's decisions. A few MB per hour of play. For analysing and improving the control.
Panel.Title: Traffic Lights & Lanes
Panel.Unavailable: The game has changed in a way TLL does not recognise. All traffic lights are left to the game.
Panel.Failed: TLL ran into an error and gave all traffic lights back to the game. Details are in Logs/TLL.log.
Panel.Conflict: this mod drives the traffic lights as well. TLL stays off while it is loaded.
Panel.ConflictUnknown: Another mod drives the traffic lights as well. TLL stays off while it is loaded.
Panel.NoProblems: No junction with long queues measured so far.
Panel.LaneToolActive: Click a lane leading in, then one leading out…
Panel.LaneToolHint: Blue circles: lanes leading into the junction. Green: lanes leading out. A click on blue picks a lane; a click on green connects it with the picked one, or takes the connection away. Red dashes mark a connection the game builds and that was taken away. A connection you added disappears entirely when taken away, as the game builds none there. Right click: drop the picked lane, then close the tool.
Panel.LaneLegendAdded: added by you; a click removes it entirely
Panel.LaneLegendRemoved: taken away; a click connects it again
Panel.LaneLegendForbidden: turn forbidden, see the list below
Panel.TurnsHint: Every way to leave the junction. A click on the rule switches between the autopilot, forbidden by you and allowed by you. Route finding avoids forbidden turns; a vehicle with no other way still takes them. At signals they get no green of their own.
TurnStateHint.Allowed: Allowed. The autopilot may forbid the turn where that relieves the junction more than the detours cost. Click: forbid.
TurnStateHint.ForbiddenByAutopilot: The autopilot forbade the turn, because it costs the junction more waiting time than the detours. The figure is the traffic it had before. Click: allow.
TurnStateHint.ForbiddenByPlayer: Forbidden by you. The autopilot leaves it. Click: allow.
TurnStateHint.AllowedByPlayer: Allowed by you. The autopilot does not forbid it. Click: leave it to the autopilot again.
TurnStateHint.ForbiddenByGame: A road upgrade of the game forbids this turn. Change it with the game's upgrade tool.
Panel.SignsHint: The sign on each approach. Without a choice of yours the game's rule applies: side roads give way to bigger roads, otherwise right before left. The game puts up matching signs and stop lines.
SignHint.Game: The autopilot sets a priority road where one pair of approaches carries most of the traffic; elsewhere the game decides by the kind of road. Once you choose a sign on an approach, the junction is left to you.
SignHint.Priority: Vehicles from this approach go before those without a priority road. Among themselves, left turns wait for oncoming traffic.
SignHint.Yield: Vehicles from this approach give way to all others.
SignHint.Stop: Vehicles from this approach stop at the line, then give way to all others.
Panel.CoordinatedNote: Runs in a green wave: a fixed cycle shared with its neighbours, side roads only on demand, and the main road gives up its green early when nobody comes. Choose another mode to take the junction out.
Panel.ClusterNote: Runs in a cluster: the roads to its neighbours are too short for the queue of a red, so the junctions share one cycle. The offsets let the side roads turn onto a main road that is green ahead. A green into a full road waits, and the junction ahead empties it first. Choose another mode to take the junction out.
Panel.PickJunction: Pick a junction on the map
Panel.VanillaSignals: The game controls these traffic lights.
Panel.Roundabout: A roundabout: traffic entering gives way to traffic in the ring. Traffic lights are not used here.
Panel.NoSignals: This junction has no traffic lights. Add them with the game's intersection upgrade.
Panel.TooQuiet: too little traffic to compare layouts
Panel.CollectingHint: The first estimate comes with the autopilot's next round, every 22.5 game minutes.
Panel.EstimateHint: Expected mean wait per layout. A dot (•) means the junction has run this layout and the estimate is corrected by what it measured. Red: it does not cope, by measurement or estimate. The autopilot changes only when another layout is clearly better, at once when a queue does not clear.
Panel.WaveBan: Kept out of green waves for
Panel.RemoveSignals: Priority rules would mean less waiting here than signals.
Panel.ProblemsHint: Junctions where queues build up in the rush hour, measured over game days. Click one to go there.
Panel.NoticesTitle: Plans TLL changed after a road changed
Panel.NoticesHint: Junctions with a plan of yours whose roads were rebuilt. TLL carried the plan over to the new roads; where that was not possible, it made a new one. They are marked on the map in violet until you have looked. Click one to go there.
Panel.NoticeAdapted: Your plan was adapted to the changed roads. Ways through the junction
Panel.NoticeReplaced: Your plan no longer fitted the changed roads and was replaced by a generated one.
Panel.ScrambleHint: A phase only for pedestrians, in all directions. Pedestrians then no longer cross alongside the vehicles, and the vehicle phases are planned without crosswalks; whoever presses the button gets the phase once per cycle. At automatic junctions the autopilot switches it on or off by the waiting time, compared with every layout. The number shows in how many of the last 8 vehicle greens turning vehicles had to wait for pedestrians.
Panel.TurnOnRedHint: Right turns (left turns in left-hand traffic) stop at red and go when the way is clear. Only where they meet nothing but traffic they give way to, and never during a pedestrian scramble. At automatic junctions the autopilot decides, if the setting allows it.
Panel.MakeAutomaticHint: The junction gets the automatic control and a generated phase plan again, the autopilot tunes it, and it can join a green wave again. Measured traffic is kept.
Panel.NothingSelected: Pick a junction to see and change its signals.
Panel.CycleHint: The cycle: one section per phase, as long as its planned green. The running phase fills up, the next one is yellow. In fixed time and green waves the line shows where in the fixed cycle the signal is.
Panel.DiagnoseHint: Writes every lane, its signal, and why the first vehicle waits, to Logs/TLL.log. Useful when vehicles stand at green.
ModeHint.Adaptive: The phase with the most pressure goes next. Green adapts to traffic and holds for arriving platoons.
ModeHint.Actuated: Fixed order. Phases without demand are skipped, green ends when the queue is gone.
ModeHint.FixedTime: Fixed greens, adjusted to the measured traffic every few minutes.
ModeHint.Flashing: Signals off, flashing yellow. The main road passes, the side roads give way.
ModeHint.Drain: Every green runs until its queue has left, at most 90 s. It ends earlier only when the exit backs up. No other phase cuts it short; the pressure only decides which goes next.
StrategyHint.Permissive: Oncoming traffic runs together, turning traffic waits for a gap.
StrategyHint.ProtectedTurns: Turns across oncoming traffic get their own green.
StrategyHint.ExclusivePedestrian: An extra phase only for pedestrians, in all directions.
Panel.OpenPlannerHint: Opens the planner: set up this junction's phases and times yourself, from templates, presets or arrow by arrow. Nothing changes on the road until you apply it.
Planner.Title: Planner
Planner.TemplatesHint: Ready-made plans, drawn on this junction, with the waiting time each would mean for its traffic.
Planner.PresetsHint: Your saved plans. They work in every city, on every junction of the same shape.
Planner.CopyHint: Puts this plan on the clipboard. Paste it at another junction, or share it in a chat. Key: Ctrl+C.
Planner.PasteHint: Loads a plan from the clipboard, copied at another junction or shared by someone. It is turned to fit, and nothing changes on the road until you apply it. Key: Ctrl+V.
Planner.UndoHint: Takes back the last change. Key: Ctrl+Z.
Planner.RedoHint: Does again what Undo took back. Key: Ctrl+Y.
Planner.OwnerHint.Autopilot: The autopilot chooses phases, times and lanes from the measured traffic, as at every automatic junction.
Planner.OwnerHint.Layout: The phases are yours. TLL keeps fitting their times to the traffic.
Planner.OwnerHint.Everything: Phases and times are yours. Nothing changes without you.
Planner.AutopilotNote: The autopilot plans this junction. Click an arrow or pick a template to take it over.
Planner.WaveNote: Applying takes this junction out of its green wave.
Planner.WaveStays: The junction stays in its green wave, which sets its times, as long as a phase carries the wave's traffic.
Planner.Tour1Text: Lanes, phases, times: the order a traffic planner works in. Jump between them freely.
Planner.Tour2Text: In a phase, a click on an arrow gives it green, another click takes it away. What would crash is refused, with the reason and where it fits instead.
Planner.Tour3Text: Your changes wait for Apply, and the check below says what still needs fixing. With Live changes on, they reach the traffic at once.
Planner.AddPhaseHint: A new, empty phase after the selected one. Fill it by clicking arrows.
Planner.MoveEarlier: Runs earlier in the cycle. In the adaptive and drain modes the demand decides the order.
Planner.MoveLater: Runs later in the cycle. In the adaptive and drain modes the demand decides the order.
Planner.FillUpHint: Adds every movement that can run in this phase without crossing another.
Planner.HoldHint: Keeps this phase green on the road while the planner is open, to watch it. Only for a phase the junction runs as it is; apply first.
Planner.ClickHint: Click an arrow to give it green in this phase. Click again to take it away.
Planner.NoGreenYetHint: Ways through the junction that no phase gives green. A click puts one where it fits best.
Planner.AutoTimingHint: TLL fits the greens to the measured traffic. Setting a time by hand switches this off, since TLL would change it again.
Planner.CycleHint: One round of all phases: each as long as its green (in fixed time) or its longest green, with yellow and all red after it.
Planner.GreenHint: How long the phase stays green in every cycle. A phase with a crosswalk gets at least what people need to cross.
Planner.MinHint: The shortest green, even when the queue is gone earlier.
Planner.MaxHint: The longest green, even when traffic keeps coming. The other phases wait at most this long for it.
Planner.PlanHint: The signal timing plan traffic engineers use: one row per way through the junction, its green over the cycle.
Planner.MaxWaitHint: A phase that has waited this long gets green next, whatever the others' queues.
Planner.Scramble: Pedestrians only in their own phase
Planner.ScrambleHint: People cross only in a phase of crosswalks alone, in all directions at once. Turning traffic then never waits for them.
Planner.TurnsNote: Allowing or forbidding a turn changes the junction's lanes at once. A plan you have not applied is loaded again then.
Planner.ExactLanes: Connect single lanes on the map
Planner.TemplatesNote: Drawn on this junction. A click loads one into your plan; nothing changes on the road until you apply it.
Planner.MainRoadHint: The road whose turns count as the main road's. TLL takes the one with the most lanes unless you choose.
Planner.WithScramble: With a phase for pedestrians alone
Planner.Template.ProtectedMainRoad: Protected turns on the main road
Planner.TemplateHint.TurnsGiveWay: Oncoming traffic runs together; turns across it wait for gaps. Fewest phases, shortest waits while traffic is light.
Planner.TemplateHint.ProtectedFirst: Turns across oncoming traffic get a green of their own, before the straight traffic of their road.
Planner.TemplateHint.ProtectedLast: Turns across oncoming traffic get a green of their own, after the straight traffic of their road.
Planner.TemplateHint.ProtectedMainRoad: Only the main road's turns get a green of their own; the side road's give way.
Planner.TemplateHint.EachRoadAlone: Every road gets green on its own. Nobody gives way to anybody, and everyone waits longest.
Planner.PresetsNote: Your saved plans, in every city. One fits every junction of the same shape, turned if needed.
Planner.WithTimesHint: Saves the mode and the greens along with the phases. Without them, a junction keeps its own.
Planner.TurnHint: The preset fits this junction more than one way. Each click lays it on the next way round.
Planner.NoPresets: No presets yet. Save the plan of a junction to use it at others.
Planner.ShareHint: Puts the preset on the clipboard as text, to post it in a chat or a forum.
Planner.Message.Reloaded: The junction's roads changed. The planner loaded it again.
Planner.Message.CannotApply: The plan still has an error. Fix it first.
Planner.Message.PlanFull: The plan has 16 phases, the most the game allows.
Planner.Message.PresetNotSaved: This preset could not be saved:
Planner.Message.PresetDoesNotFit: This preset does not fit the junction:
Planner.Message.PresetLoadedTurnable: Loaded. It fits more than one way; turn it if the roads are wrong:
Planner.Message.PresetCopied: On the clipboard, ready to share:
Planner.Message.Copied: The plan is on the clipboard. Paste it at another junction.
Planner.Message.PasteNothing: The clipboard holds no TLL preset.
Planner.AllGood: Every way through the junction gets green, and no paths cross.
Planner.Check.NoGreen: green in no phase. Its traffic would wait forever.
Planner.Check.SplitLane: one lane, different greens. The first car blocks the others.
Planner.Check.TooMany: More than 16 phases. The game has no more signal groups; delete or merge phases.
Planner.Check.LongCycle2: Everyone waits long at red; shorter maxima help.
Planner.LiveHint: Every change reaches the traffic at once, without Apply. A plan with an error waits until it is fixed. The switch is the same for every junction. Without it, Ctrl+Enter applies.
Planner.ApplyBlocked: Fix the errors the check shows first.
Planner.LanesHint: Which lane of each road leads where, as the arrows painted on the road. A turn with a lane of its own can get a green of its own.
Planner.NoLaneChoice: No road here has more than one lane leading in, so there are no arrows to choose.
Planner.GameLanesHint: Gives this road the lanes the game builds by itself, without your rules or the autopilot's.
Planner.PickLane: Click a lane to change where it leads.
Planner.SuggestionHint: The lanes the autopilot would choose for the measured traffic: the busiest lane carries less.
Planner.LaneEdit.LastDirection: A lane has to lead somewhere.
Planner.LaneEdit.Gap: A lane serves neighbouring directions only.
Planner.LaneEdit.Cross: The paths of two lanes would cross.
Planner.LaneEdit.Uncovered: This direction would lose its last lane.
Planner.LaneEdit.TooMany: The road it leads into has fewer lanes.
Planner.Message.LaneLastDirection: A lane has to lead somewhere.
Planner.Message.LaneGap: A lane serves neighbouring directions only.
Planner.Message.LaneCross: The paths of two lanes would cross.
Planner.Message.LaneUncovered: This direction would lose its last lane.
Planner.Message.LaneTooMany: The road it leads into has fewer lanes.
Planner.SolidHint: On the last road pieces before the junction, drivers keep their lane. They pick it before the lines instead of cutting in at the last moment. The game has no hard ban: a driver in the wrong lane may still change, at a high cost, so nobody gets stuck.
Planner.SolidNote: Drivers choose their lane before the solid lines and keep it there.
Planner.SolidStepHint: How far back from the stop line, in whole road pieces, as far as the road goes before the previous junction.
Planner.SharesLane: It shares a lane with other directions and goes only with them.
Planner.WithLanesHint: Saves the lane arrows and solid lines along with the phases, for roads with as many lanes as here.
Panel.JunctionTypeHint: What regulates this junction. A click opens the game's own tool for it; click the junction on the map, and the game builds it at the price of its road menu.
Panel.RoundaboutStays: A roundabout goes with the bulldozer.
Panel.ClickJunction: Click the junction on the map. The game shows the price and builds it.
Panel.PlanKept: Your signal plan is kept. It runs again when the junction gets traffic lights.
Panel.CrosswalksHint: Opens the game's crosswalk upgrade. Each click where a road meets the junction adds its crosswalk or takes it away. The planner shows the crosswalks as ways through the junction that need green.
Panel.ClickCrosswalk: Click where a road meets the junction to add its crosswalk there, or take it away.
JunctionTypeHint.RightOfWay: No lights, no stop signs: the side road gives way, or the signs you set.
JunctionTypeHint.AllWayStop: Everyone stops, then goes in the order they came. Fair and slow; for quiet junctions with even traffic.
JunctionTypeHint.TrafficLights: Signals, which TLL can run and you can plan in the planner.
JunctionTypeHint.Roundabout: Traffic in the ring has right of way. Pick a size; the game checks whether it fits.
